message.content:
Here’s a quick‑look “horror movie buffet” spanning classic chills, modern dread, psychological nightmares, and everything in between. Pick whatever mood strikes—whether you want an old‑school scream fest or something that will keep your brain racing long after the credits roll.

| # | Title (Year) | Subgenre / Theme | Why it matters |
|---|--------------|------------------|---------------|
| **1** | *Psycho* (1960) | Psychological thriller/Slasher | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense & the iconic shower scene still sets the bar for terror. |
| **2** | *Halloween* (1978) | Slasher | Introduced Michael Myers and the idea that evil can lurk behind suburban normalcy. |
| **3** | *The Shining* (1980) | Supernatural / Isolation | Kubrick turns a haunted hotel into a labyrinthine nightmare; great for fans of atmospheric creepiness. |
| **4** | *A Nightmare on Elm Street* (1984) | Dream‑based horror | Freddy Krueger shows how fear can invade even our sleep. |
| **5** | *Candyman* (1992) | Urban legend / Social commentary | A chilling look at mythmaking and racism wrapped in a haunting story. |
| **6** | *Scream* (1996) | Meta‑slasher | Revives the genre while poking fun at its own tropes—a smart, self‑aware scarefest. |
| **7** | *Hereditary* (2018) | Family trauma + cosmic horror | An unsettling blend of domestic drama and eldritch dread that keeps viewers guessing. |
| **8** | *Get Out* (2017) | Horror + social satire | Jordan Peele uses body horror as a vehicle for sharp racial critique. |
| **9** | *Midsommar* (2019) | Folk horror | Daylight doesn’t always mean safety; this film flips daylight horrors onto bright Swedish summer. |
| **10** | *It Follows* (2014) | Modern folklore | Simple premise – a curse passed through sex – turned into relentless paranoia. |
| **11** | *The Babadook* (2014) | Psychological monster | A mother‑son relationship spirals into a literal manifestation of grief. |
| **12** | *Paranormal Activity* (2007) | Found footage | Low budget meets high tension; perfect for those who love jump scares without CGI overkill. |
| **13** | *Us* (2019) | Duality + family horror | Another Peele gem where doppelgängers turn a vacation home into a nightmarish battlefield. |
| **14** | *The Witch* (2015) | Period folk horror | Slow burn, period detail, and a creeping sense of isolation make this one unforgettable. |
| **15** | *Evil Dead II* (1987) | Campy gore | If you’re looking for laughs mixed with blood‑splatter, this cult favorite delivers. |

### Quick Streaming Guide (as of early 2026)

| Platform | Notable Titles Available |
|----------|---------------------------|
| **Netflix** | *The Haunting of Hill House*, *His Dark Materials* (for spooky vibes), *The Conjuring* series |
| **Amazon Prime Video** | *Hereditary*, *Midsommar*, *The Lodge* |
| **HBO Max** | *The Ring*, *Sinister*, *Creepshow* anthology |
| **Disney+** | *Haunted Mansion* (live‑action), *Coraline* (animated horror) |
| **Apple TV+** | *The Twilight Zone* revival episodes featuring horror stories |
| **Shudder** (subscription only) | Full catalog of indie and mainstream horror including all above plus many more niche gems |

> **Tip:** For the best experience, pair a good popcorn bowl with a dark room—and maybe a friend who won’t run away when the lights flicker!

Enjoy the fright! 🎃
